name: uw-course-lookup
summary: Grades, seats and a degree-aware timetable planner for every Fall 2026 UW–Madison course

shot.alt: Course list with a grade band across the top, filter lenses, and a GPA bar, trend and open seats for each course

hook: Grade history, instructor GPAs and seats for all 4,438 Fall 2026 UW–Madison courses, plus a timetable planner that knows your degree.
built: Vanilla JS, Cloudflare Workers and Workers AI, SQLite, GitHub Actions CI

notes: A sticky A–F band morphs into whichever course you hover, with ticks marking the campus-wide split, so every row reads against the baseline.
Lenses such as Instructor matters, a dot plot of every instructor’s GPA, saved plans, side-by-side compare, and an assistant that can search courses and build a timetable.

pages.title: The planner
notes: Pick one of 212 degree programs and drop in your transcript or DARS. The file is read in the browser, not uploaded, and the planner shows what is done, in progress and left.

It searches for conflict-free timetables over each course’s real enrollment packages (a lecture plus its discussion), honoring early starts, days off and seat availability, and returns six options with an .ics export.
If the request is impossible it says why, for example two required courses that always overlap.
pages.caption: The solver is a plain module with no DOM or network access, so the page, a Web Worker and the Node tests run the same code. It returns the best result it found, not a proof of optimality.

pages.title: How it works
notes: The page holds no course data. A Cloudflare Worker serves one page of results at a time to a browser that has passed an invisible human check.
Each visitor and each network has a daily allowance counted in course records. Requests are rate-limited and logged, never the assistant conversation, and CI fails if a private file is committed.
No endpoint returns the dataset in bulk. That raises the cost of copying everything; it cannot prevent it.
pages.caption: Build and serve. The data files are gitignored; the page, the Worker and the pipeline are public.

pages.title: What the data says
notes: Instructor beats course. In MATH 320 the most and least generous instructors, each with 200+ graded students, sit 1.67 GPA points apart on the same syllabus.
How often a course comes up in chat says nothing about its grade (ρ = −0.07, n = 215). The tone of its Reddit threads does (ρ = +0.43, n = 220).
pages.caption: The eight largest gaps between the lowest and highest instructor GPA in one course, among 290 tracked courses. Each instructor has at least 30 graded students.

blurb: UW–Madison course lookup: grade history, seats and a degree-aware timetable planner
